text: About a month afterward, the Prefect paid us another visit and admitted that, although he had searched the house again, he had found nothing. <break time="0.8s" /> The reward had become very large, he said, and he would gladly give fifty thousand francs to anyone who could help him. <break time="0.8s" /> In that case, said Dupin calmly, you may write me a check for that amount, and I will hand you the letter. <break time="0.8s" /> The Prefect sat speechless for some moments, staring at my friend with his mouth open, as if he could not believe his ears. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, after several long pauses, he signed the check, and Dupin, unlocking a desk, took out the letter and handed it over. <break time="0.8s" /> The Prefect seized it with wild joy and, his hand trembling, glanced at it before rushing out without a single word. <break time="0.8s" /> When he had gone, Dupin explained that the Paris police were skillful in their own way, but their methods did not suit this man. <break time="0.8s" /> He then told me about an eight year old schoolboy who was famous for always winning a marble game called even and odd. <break time="0.8s" /> Before each guess, the boy would make his face look like his opponents, and he would notice what thoughts arose in his own mind.
